passage: Tuition centre supervisor's note. Imran has taught two evening batches since August, and I noticed something unusual on payment days. Most of the young tutors go straight to the canteen. Imran opens a small notebook, takes out a third of the envelope and puts it into a tin marked "exams and emergencies". The rest is spent without guilt on food, bus fare and a film. Simran, a fellow tutor, asked about it and Imran said, "Then I never have to decide what to do with the whole amount." In October a sudden lab fee came up and Imran paid it from the tin without borrowing. I did not comment, but I have started suggesting the tin idea to the newer staff.

qa.q: What is written on the tin where Imran puts a third of each payment?
qa.a: The tin is marked exams and emergencies.

qa.q: What did Imran feel about spending the rest?
qa.a: Imran spent the rest without guilt, sure that the saved third was already set aside.

qa.q: What could Imran do if the tin fills up, and why?
qa.a: Imran could decide on a second small target such as books, because the habit stays the same while the goal changes.

qa.q: How might the supervisor see Imran's habit compared with other tutors?
qa.a: The supervisor seems impressed and a little surprised, and has started suggesting the idea to newer staff.

grounding: A student saves a fixed share of every payment for exam fees and emergencies and spends the rest, making income a steady support.

subtype: Approach: saving a fixed share as a buffer [Action]
passage:
Friday, 9 p.m. (Preeti's diary)
Got ₹3,600 from the Class 8 tuition today. Before I could even think about the jacket in the Sarojini lane, I did what Vandana Masi told me to try in April: ₹1,200 straight into the steel box marked 'fees + emergencies', the rest in my wallet.
Four months of this now. The box has ₹3,700, even after paying my exam form fee last month without asking Papa. That felt good in a quiet way.
The first weeks were annoying. I'd look at the box and think of momos. Now I don't open it unless it's real.
Today Isha from class borrowed my notes and said she was broke again, three days after her payment came in. I didn't lecture her. I just remembered being exactly that.
Jacket next month, maybe. From the other two-thirds.

qa.q: How much went into the steel box today?
How does Preeti feel about the box now compared with the first weeks?
qa.a: At first it felt annoying and tempting, but now there is a quiet pride and calm in having money ready for real needs.

qa.q: What else could help Preeti keep the box working when the jacket tempts again?
qa.a: Deciding in advance what counts as 'real' for opening it, and talking to Vandana Masi if a big need comes up.

qa.q: How might Vandana Masi see the last four months?
qa.a: Vandana Masi would likely be pleased that the April idea became a habit, one that paid the exam form fee without anyone asking Papa.

grounding: Shows a student setting aside a third of every payment for fees and emergencies so earnings become steady support.
